Stellantis North America Patents New-Gen Jeep Compass in the US
19 photos
Photo: USPTO/FCA
Stellantis has recently secured US-market design protection for a Jeep model that American customers still cannot purchase. D1,157,295 S is the design patent for the new-gen Compass, which is codenamed J4U in Euro-market specification. Built in Italy at the Melfi plant on STLA Medium underpinnings from the Peugeot 3008 and Opel Grandland, this SUV may not even be sold in North America.
The United States Patent and Trademark Office granted the design patent to FCA US LLC earlier this month, following an application from February 2025. All drawings show the exterior from a bunch of angles. The squarer body of the J4U is joined by more pronounced wheel arches, pretty slim lighting elements, and a reinterpreted seven-slot grille that doesn't look Jeep enough if you ask me.
Meanwhile, American dealer lots still get the second-generation Compass. Identified as MP, this fellow entered model year 2027 with little in the way of changes from 2026. Prices kick off at $29,900 as of this writing, and prospective customers are offered five choices. All come with 2.0-liter turbo inline-four muscle and all-wheel drive, albeit not every AWD system is created equal.
Active Drive is the lesser of two all-wheel-drive systems. Standard on four grades, Active Drive features a disconnecting power transfer unit, 4WD Lock mode, and on-demand operation. Most of the time, the American Compass is front-wheel drive to maximize fuel economy. Exclusive to the Trailhawk, the Active Drive Low system rocks a two-speed PTU and a shorter final drive ratio.
Engaging 4WD Low in the Trailhawk locks the front and rear axles together, and 20:1 is the advertised crawl ratio. Rock mode and Hill Descent Control are other highlights that make this grade stand out in the crowd. Regardless of grade, the Compass for North America packs 200 horsepower and an eight-speed auto.
Photo: Jeep The J4U for Europe is longer than its predecessor, and its 110-inch (2,795 millimeters) wheelbase provides quite a bit more room between the axles. Powertrain options kick off with a mild-hybrid I3 turbo, followed by a 1.6-liter turbo inline-four with plug-in hybrid assistance. Full-electric options are available as well, including a 4xe-branded EV with two electric drive units. The 4xe develops 375 ps (370 hp) and 577 Nm (426 lb-ft) of combined torque.
Having cleared all that up, why isn't the European Compass being adapted for North America? The answer comes from none other than Stellantis North America, which confirmed in August 2026 that Belvidere Assembly is gearing up for STLA One production. The next-generation Cherokee is listed as the first vehicle on that platform, with pilot production kicking off in 2028.
Belvidere will assemble a minimum of two vehicles on the STLA One, and the second one should be the Compass for North America. The Auburn Hills-based automaker has committed $800 million for said plant. Unfortunately, both the all-new Cherokee and Compass for America are to start production in 2029.
STLA One is likely to merge and phase out a bunch of platforms. STLA Large and STLA Frame are understood to remain untouched as the other two pillars in the automaker's strategy to put 50 percent of global volume onto three core vehicle architectures by 2030.
